audience: Designers, product engineers, and teams building AI agents who need real interface references they are allowed to trust.
problem: Screenshot libraries show pictures of interfaces with no way to tell what was measured, where the media came from, or whether the numbers attached to them mean anything. A designer quoting a pattern cannot say what evidence stands behind it.
promise: Every record states its source, hashes, provenance class, and measured state — complete or partial — so you can cite the reference and its evidence together.

hero.headline: Spis — interface references you can cite
hero.lede: An open corpus of {{record_count}} real-interface records across {{catalog_count}} families. Every record states its source, hashes, provenance class, and measured state, so the reference and its evidence travel together.

secondaryAction.label: Read the evidence contract
secondaryAction.purpose: Inspect the rules every record must meet before it exists.

approvedClaims.claim: Spis indexes 13 catalogs and 700 third-party records across iOS, Android, macOS, desktop, web, dashboard, terminal, CLI, onboarding, documentation, store-listing, design-system, and report-evidence families.
Every record carries a provenance class: captured from a local product run, a browser we drove on a Stado host, or media published by the owner.
Catalogs are generated from records and refuse to render when index, records, and files disagree.
A missing observation is recorded as an evidence gap and is never promoted into prose.
The corpus is Apache-2.0 licensed and content owners can remove or relink their media at any time.

requiredProof: terminal transcript of bin/spis catalogs --check passing over the generated index

rules: Use canonical Wisent design tokens; no new palette.
No customer logos, testimonials, or invented dashboards.
